text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Finance Minister Mohieddin el-Gharib tells a taxation conference that Egypt will have a new customs system within the next three months and will adjust the sales tax on certain goods. Government will use part of its privatisation revenue to develop the new valley. The fourth biggest financial institution in the world has offered to issue Egyptian shares and bonds in international markets.
- Government to support the private sector in a drive to increase cotton exports.
- Economy Minister Nawal el-Tatawi says President Hosni Mubarak's trip to the United States in March will be a follow-up for deals signed during the Cairo economic conference.
- Egypt and Malta to sign accord soon to scrap dual taxation and protect their industries.
- A message to Mubarak from the president of Malta. Maltese foreign minister says that Egypt has a big role in the security of the Mediterranean.
- Government sets price of Giza 45 cotton variety at 1,000 pounds ($295) before it is planted. It also sets price of one ardab (5.44 bushels) of wheat at 95 pounds.
- Ganzouri tells parliament: Emergency law will protect Egypt's potential and its economic achievements. The government will cherish the people's freedoms.
- FBI director after meeting Mubarak says relations with Egyptian Interior Ministry are good.
